note: Flagged for Review. These items do NOT block the merge (per the brief). Each item lists the source to check. Status 'Unverified' means the value could not be confirmed from an official source, so it was left blank or marked, not filled in.

rows.item: Lamar Jackson absence is given as 6-9 weeks (NFL Network headline) and as 6-10 weeks (NFL.com roundup, Nov 13).

rows.item: Jacob Hummel (HOU LB) is linked to the nfl.com slug 'jake-hummel', which differs from the listed first name.

rows.item: Injury rows are limited to players with an injury entry or a game status. Players with neither are not listed.
rows.why: Scope decision, not an error. Full list is on the report page.

rows.item: Secondary sources disagree on whether online sports betting is authorised in Mexico. Some say it is legal under a SEGOB permit holder; others say online operation needs a separate DGJS authorisation; one says online gambling is 'legal' with ~30 licensed operators (S14). The official 1947 law text reviewed (S05) contains no online provision in the articles read.
rows.why: No official SEGOB statement was retrieved. No operator counts or tax rates were used.

rows.item: The Cámara ficha lists 'Sin reforma' (no amending decrees). Secondary sources cite a regulation reform of 16 Nov 2023 and a law reform announced in Sep 2026.
rows.why: Could not confirm either reform from an official source. Not used.

rows.item: The NFL gambling policy text and the Nov 2025 prop-bet memo were not retrieved from an official source. Quotes come from ESPN, Philadelphia Inquirer and MLive.
rows.why: Official NFL gambling-policy and November 2025 prop-memo text was not retrieved. S04 is only an official search starting point; the cited quotations/reporting remain secondary and unverified.

rows.item: The 2017 NFL Personnel (Injury) Report Policy cited by secondary sources was not retrieved. Definitions (Out / Doubtful / Questionable) and the Wed-Fri schedule come from secondary sources.
rows.why: Definitions match the secondary sources but are not confirmed from the primary policy.

rows.item: 46 active players per game and 90-minute inactive deadline come from secondary sources only.
rows.why: Not confirmed from the 2026 NFL Rulebook or the CBA.

rows.item: Kickoff times for games other than the 2026 Week 10 schedule page sections read come from the time headers on the injury report page (NFL.com).
rows.why: Both pages are NFL.com; the schedule page was only partly read. Times are ET as published.

rows.item: No local-time conversion is published by this site; NFL injury/game times remain labelled as source-published ET. No UTC offset is asserted.
rows.why: A local-time preference and conversion are not needed for the current tables and have not been added.

rows.item: Repo has no README content, no source code, no .gitignore, and no CI workflow.
rows.why: Recorded for review; see repo review R-02, R-03.

rows.item: Brief's session-<id>/<task> branch naming conflicts with Arena's single-branch rule.
rows.why: Followed Arena rule (R-04).

rows.item: The 160 injury rows were transcribed by hand from the NFL.com report text fetched on 2026-11-14 (no automated parser). Totals (66 Out, 10 Doubtful, 84 Questionable) are computed from the file, not typed.
rows.why: Manual transcription can contain typos. Each row links to its player page so it can be checked one by one.

rows.item: The NFL Support odds-widget FAQ lists FanDuel, Caesars, and DraftKings; the 2026 sportsbook-partnership announcement names DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics Betting and Gaming.
rows.why: Both pages are official but may describe different widgets, partners, or periods. Do not treat the lists as interchangeable or as an odds API, price history, or data licence.
rows.status: Unverified for a specific widget/provider; no market feed used

rows.item: Three public files carry row-level player data for Week 10 injuries: data/injuries_w10_2026.json (160 rows), data/injuries_week10_2026.json (75 rows) and data/signals/injuries_week10_2026.json (76 rows, shown on the Signals page).
rows.why: NFL.com Terms s.1.3 prohibit systematic retrieval, and compiling a database from the Services, without express prior written consent. The public injuries page (pages/injuries.html, table tbl-players) still renders the player-level table built from data/injuries_w10_2026.json (160 rows). data/injuries_week10_2026.json (75 rows) and data/signals/injuries_week10_2026.json (76 rows, read by the Signals page) are also public. This session did NOT change those pages; it only added the private raw layer and counts-only summary. Git history keeps earlier copies.
rows.status: Open - reviewer decision: remove the row-level tables and files, or confirm permission in writing. Not changed in this session (outside claim).

rows.item: The earlier public table (data/injuries_w10_2026.json, read 2026-11-14) has no section for LAC or BAL, so 12 designated players are missing, and it lists IND's Arden Key as Questionable. The 16 Nov page shows Arden Key with no game status.
rows.why: Coverage gap plus one status difference. Counts were corrected on the public page from the 16 Nov transcription (347 rows, 28 clubs). The earlier file is kept, marked superseded, because it is used for the delta.
rows.status: Corrected in counts; earlier file superseded (see F-20)

rows.item: Brief claims VR-04 to VR-07: published 254 rows and 4 no-injury sections versus live 279 rows and 2 sections; Seattle and Cincinnati shown injury-free while listing 15 and 4 players.
rows.why: Not reproduced. The repo table had 160 rows and showed Seattle and Cincinnati with 4 designated players each. The 16 Nov page lists 347 player rows across 28 club sections, and every section has at least one injury entry or game status. Neither 254 nor 279 could be matched to any capture. No brief figure was adopted.
rows.status: Not reproduced - reviewer to supply the capture that gave 279 rows

rows.item: Brief claims VR-08: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed have blank game status on the published table.
rows.why: Not reproduced. The repo table already shows Out for all three, and the 16 Nov page shows Out for all three.

rows.item: The 16 Nov capture was read after most Week 10 games had finished: the schedule page shows 12 Finals, PIT-CIN live in Q1, and LAC-BAL still to play.
rows.why: Game-status and practice fields on the page may reflect post-game state, not the pre-kickoff status a forecast needs. The 16 Nov capture cannot be used as a pre-kickoff snapshot.
rows.status: Open - a pre-kickoff capture is needed for any forecast

rows.item: The official page uses AZ for Arizona. The earlier root table used ARI.
rows.why: Normalised in the counts (ARI mapped to AZ for the delta). The Signals table also uses AZ.

rows.item: The injury report does not list players on injured reserve. Headlines on the official page report IR moves for Ravens QB Lamar Jackson and Dolphins QB Malik Willis. Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson is on the page as Out with Illness (row confirmed in the transcription).
rows.why: Absence from the report does not mean available. No reserve or transactions list has been captured, so IR status is headline-level only and the Willis headline was not re-read this session.
rows.status: Open - capture the official reserve/transaction list

rows.item: private/captures/nfl_injuries_w10_2026_reg10.psv holds 347 rows transcribed by hand from the fetch tool output. The raw fetch bytes were not kept, so the stored SHA-256 is a hash of the transcription, not of the NFL page.
rows.why: A transcription hash proves the file has not changed since capture; it does not prove the rows match the page byte for byte. Two transcription faults were found and fixed during validation (an extra delimiter; the Cardinals code). The file is git-ignored and is not on the site.
rows.status: Open - reviewer may re-read the page to confirm any row

rows.item: The Signals injury table (signals/injuries.html, 76 rows) omits three Arizona Out rows and all LAC and BAL rows that are designated on the 16 Nov page.
rows.why: Another section's data. Not edited in this session (coordination rule: log requests instead of editing another section's files). It also shows player names, which conflicts with the private-layer requirement (see F-20).
rows.status: Request logged in COORDINATION.md for the Signals owner

rows.item: The brief refers to a 136-game log. The repo has no game-level log. data/league_state.json holds a consistency check only (136 wins, 136 losses, one tied game).
rows.why: A consistency sum cannot be used as a corpus. A corpus needs every game's official result, and closing lines (none exist: PP-01). Season-long pulls would need terms consent (S29 s.1.3).

rows.item: Brief claims about starters and depth (Lock, McCord, Brissett VR-24/25 and VQ-05; Baltimore QB rows VR-17/26 and VQ-07; Colts receiver trades; Texans and Packers depth pages) are not verified here.

The headline text about who starts was not re-read this session and is not used. No depth chart or transaction log was captured, so no depth row is verified.
